proposals.title: Debrief and Rematch: every point you lost, by misconception, won back 48 hours later
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: after a contest they don't just look at a rank. They see which named misconceptions and which time decisions cost how many points. They study one worked twin per trap straight away. Two days later they sit a Rematch: fresh numbers, the same traps. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: feedback on the named error, then a worked example, then retrieval spaced out on new numbers is the highest-yield way to fix an error. Calling it 'winning points back' gives a reason to do it.

RESULT PANEL (contest page section 4 and the contest-mode summary), a new block after the tiles: h2 'Points left on the table · 90 of 260'. Rows are sorted by points, largest first:
(a) One row per missed question, grouped by trap norm: 'Used the diameter as the radius · Q7 · hard · −30'. Skips read 'Skipped · Q9 · medium · −20'. Voids read 'Voided · Q4 · −20'. A grid-in with no named reason reads 'Grid-in · Q8 · Circles · −20'.
(b) 'Pace · 3 right answers over pace par · −15'.
(c) 'Finish bonus · 1 skipped · −10'.
The rows sum to max − points.

Each misconception row has a quiet 'Fix it · 3' that opens an inline drill (R23 inline, R24 cfg.inline):
- Item 1 is a WORKED TWIN: a fresh seed of the same template drawn with want={template: that reason}. It is shown in review mode with the key, the trap option labelled with the misconception, and the rationale. Button 'Got it'.
- Items 2 and 3 are twins to solve, with the same want.

REMATCH: created at finish as a contests row.
- Kind 'rematch', id 'rematch-{sid}', owner = the learner.
- opens = finished + 48 h, closes = opens + 7 days.
- spec.slots = one [template, tier, fmt, want] per missed, skipped or voided slot, plus 2 twins of slots answered right, which disguise the set and add spaced review. The set is shuffled, max 8 questions.
- Rematches that come due within the same 24 h merge into one set (max 12), so misses from different contests are interleaved.
- Runner: practice session in contest mode, key after each question, answer clock at pace par per question. Unranked and unrated.
- A right answer is a clean answer (R8). It closes the trap, and R9 then schedules check-ins at 3, 10 and 30 days. A miss keeps the trap open and requeues that item into the next Rematch 3 days later. After 2 misses it leaves the item to Review's Redo.
- The Rematch result reads 'Won back 70 of 90 points', with one row per original question: ✓ or ✗ now, against its original mark.

SURFACES:
- Overview Contests › Live: a row with a circular-arrow icon, 'Rematch · Tue's Daily · 5 questions · closes Mon'.
- Upcoming: 'opens Thu 4:10 PM'.
- Today's challenge card: 'Rematch ready · 5'.
- Up next (U1): a row.
- Your rankings › Contest history: a new 'Follow-up' column reading 'Won back 70/90', 'Opens Thu' or '—'.
- Achievements (R25): 'Won back' ladder at 10 / 50 / 200 questions.

DATA: result.left = [{kind: trap|skip|void|pace|finish, qid, template, norm, label, tier, points}], computed in compete.finish_contest from the marks, attempts.reason/norm and tier points.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A daily with 2 wrong answers (different reasons) and 1 skip gives result.left with 3 question rows whose points equal their tier points.
- GET /api/contests?status=upcoming lists 'rematch-{sid}' opening at finished + 48 h with 5 questions.
- Each Rematch question regenerates with an option whose norm equals the original's.
- Answering it right closes that trap.
proposals.beats: Their contest: 'Answers are revealed after the contest ends', and then nothing follows. Their per-contest stats are counts: Score / Correct / Incorrect / Skipped / Voided. Their wrong options are explained in prose ('Distractor Analysis') but never tagged, so they can't total points lost per misconception, serve the same trap on new numbers, or schedule a spaced retry. The spec as written has 'Practice my misses' and 'Another like this' (same template, any option), both immediate and massed. The upgrade adds the per-trap points breakdown, the worked twin, want-matched twins and the delayed, interleaved Rematch.
proposals.needs: S8: compete.finish_contest writes result.left, plus the 'rematch' contest kind and its scheduling. F5: drill 'want' and 'templates' (§2.6) and cfg.inline (R24). F3: UI.review inline mode for the worked twin (R23). F4: R8 clean answer and R9 trap close/check-ins. S4: contest mode in the practice session (R28 hooks). F2: Up next row (U1). S3: Today card line. S1: 'Won back' achievement through R25. P5 leagues read the won-back points.

proposals.title: Daily Encore: two of your own due check-ins right after the Daily
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: after the ranked ten they answer two more questions in the same sitting, about 3 minutes. These are their own fixed mistakes that are due a spaced check-in today (R9's 3/10/30 days). WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: spaced retrieval of your own errors is what makes fixes stick. Students skip check-ins because they are a separate chore. Stacking them onto the one habit a student keeps every day turns the Daily into the spacing engine.

RUNNER: when the tenth answer is filed, the sitting is finished and ranked first, so the Encore can never touch rank, points, rating or the clock. The practice session then shows an interstitial before the result panel:
- k 'ENCORE' + 'Two of your own · due today · not ranked · about 3 min';
- the two labels as rows ('Used the diameter as the radius · Circles · fixed Sep 13');
- pill 'Start encore' (Enter) and quiet 'Skip for today'.
The result panel then gets a line: 'Encore: 2 of 2 held · next check-ins Thu' with ✓/✗ per label.

PICK ORDER:
1. traps with due ≤ today (the checks pool), oldest due first;
2. then open traps by hits × recency;
3. if the student has none, the top trap of yesterday's Daily field, as a twin, tagged 'From the field'.

COUNT: prefs key 'encore' (R11 registry) ∈ {0, 2, 3, 5}, default 2. Settings › Practice renders it: 'Encore after the Daily Challenge'.

DRILL: served as {pool:'checks', ids:[trap ids], each:1, level:'as_missed', source:'encore', parent: daily sid}, cfg.inline (R24), so it is never listed as a sitting. The key and rationale show after each question. A right answer passes that check-in (checks + 1, next due). A miss reopens the trap as Relapsed (R9).

SURFACES: Today's and Overview's challenge card, once the Daily is done: chip 'Encore · 2 due' + quiet 'Do it now' if the student skipped it. Achievements (R25): 'Kept' ladder, 10 / 50 / 200 check-ins held in an Encore. League points (P5) get +20 per held check-in.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A learner with 3 traps due today finishes the daily. The next GET /api/drill/{sid} returns encore {ids: the 2 oldest due}.
- Answering one right sets that trap's checks + 1 and moves its due.
- The daily's points and rank are unchanged by the Encore.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has spaced review only for vocabulary ('Due Today' words). Math mistakes are never scheduled again, and a contest ends at a score. In the spec as written the Daily and the check-ins are separate: the Daily feeds rank, and check-ins wait in Review for a visit that daily-only students never make.
proposals.needs: F4: R9 traps.due/checks and prefs.py key 'encore'. F5: drill pool 'checks' and cfg.inline. S4: runner interstitial after finish through R28's compete.state_extra. S8: fallback pick of the field's top trap. S3: Today card chip. S1: Settings row and achievement ladder.

proposals.title: Pace trace, time sinks, pace par by tier, and a pace guide that fades by the Final
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: after every contest they see, per question, where their time went against a pace par that expects easy questions fast and hard ones slower. In the Weekly Module a live ahead/behind guide trains their internal clock. In the Season Final the guide is gone, as on the real test. They learn skip-and-return from their own numbers. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: Math points are lost to 3-minute sinks and unfinished modules as much as to content. Pacing improves only when it is measured per question, scaffolded, then faded.

PACE PAR:
- easy 60 s, medium 95 s, hard 130 s. A Daily's 3E/4M/3H sums to exactly its 950 s clock; a 7E/8M/7H module sums to 2,090 of 2,100 s.
- Once a template has ≥ 30 first-try right answers with sms/ms, its par becomes their median, clamped to its tier par ± 40%.
- compete.par(template, tier) is the one source.

RESULT PANEL, block 'Pace':
- A chart 100% × 160 px. x = question in answer order, y = cumulative minutes. Lines: you (orange), pace par (graphite dashed), field median (grey, per slot, from the whole-bank field; see parity gaps).
- Each point is a ✓/✗ glyph. Focus or hover shows 'Q7 · 3:12 · par 1:35 · ✗'.
- role=img, an aria summary and a hidden table.
- 'Time sinks' list: questions over 2× par ('Q7 · 3:12 · par 1:35 · wrong').
- Summary line: '3 time sinks took 8:20 (par 4:05). 2 were wrong: moving on at 2× par and coming back would have saved 3:40, about 2 medium questions.' Computed as Σ over wrong sinks of (time − 2 × par), divided by the medium par.
- 'Banked' line: 'Easy: median 0:41 vs par 1:00 · 2:40 banked for the hard ones.'
- Two action pills from U7: 'Speed drill · {slowest skill answered right}' and 'Careful set · {skill answered fastest and wrong}'.

WEEKLY MODULE (test window, wall clock):
- A chip beside the timer reads 'On pace' / '1:40 ahead' / '2:10 behind', from Σ par of the questions reached vs elapsed time.
- A lobby switch 'Pace guide' is on by default, and the chip's × hides it for the sitting.
- Season Final: never offered. The lobby line reads 'No pace guide: test conditions.'
- Private contests: a creator's switch.

YOUR RANKINGS › Pace: two trend rows over the last 10 contests, 'Time in sinks per contest' and 'Banked on easy'.

ACCEPTANCE:
- par sums: daily ladder = 950, module-1 blueprint = 2,090.
- A sitting with Q7 at 200 s (hard, wrong) and all else at par lists exactly one sink, and the saved-time line reads 3:20 − 2:10 × ... as computed by the formula above (a unit assert in server/checks/s8.py).
- The Final lobby has no guide switch.
proposals.beats: Their Time Analysis is one chart of average seconds per answered question by difficulty, plus 'under pressure' copy. There is no per-question trace, no par, no field line, no link to action and no guided-then-faded pacing. Their 'speed bonus' rewards raw speed. The spec as written adds medians against the field and a flat 95 s line, but it gives no per-question trace, no time-sink cost and no scaffold that fades.
proposals.needs: F4: attempts.sms, and R7 qstate.ms per question in the test window (S5 records it). F1: a line chart in charts.js. S5: the timer chip hook and lobby switch in the test window. F4: U7's progress.pace and drills for the action pills. S8: compete.par, and the field medians from the whole-bank field (parity gap 'field stats').

proposals.title: Par and your level in SAT points
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: before a contest they see their par, the base points a student at their rating is expected to score on this exact ladder. After it they see 'base 120 · par 105 · +15 over par'. Their level reads as a modelled Math band, and the next level is stated in questions. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: a raw rank tells a 480-level student they lost again. Beating par tells them they improved today, and that is what keeps them coming back. Tying the rating to the 200–800 scale makes the contest number mean their target, so they play for the goal, not the board.

PAR:
- For each slot i, E_i = 1/(1 + 10^((R_i − R_s)/400)) against item_ratings(template, tier) (seeded 900/1100/1300 as specced).
- par = Σ E_i × tier_points_i, rounded to 5, on base points only (no pace or finish bonus, stated).
- Frozen at start in sessions.result.par from the pre-sitting rating. Twins share template and tier, so everyone at one rating has one par.

SURFACES:
- Lobby: 'Your par 105 · Level 4', with helper 'what students at your rating score on these 10, on average'.
- Points tile sub-line: 'base 120 · par 105 · +15'.
- Daily and Weekly boards: a 'vs par' column.
- Leaderboard metric 'vs par': Σ (base − par) over ranked sittings in the period, min 3 sittings, ties as specced.

LEVEL LADDER (Your rankings, a table: Level | Rating | Modelled Math band | Students at it):
- The band is computed in compete.band(R). Module 1 = blueprint.slots('module1', 1) at each tier's mean item rating; expected right = Σ E. Route = upper if the expected weighted fraction ≥ scoring.ROUTE_UP_AT. Module 2 uses that route's slots. Total weighted fraction → scoring._interpolate → centre ± MOCK_HALF_BAND, with LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING applied on the lower route.
- Your row is highlighted. Label: 'Modelled from question ratings, not measured.'
- Once ≥ 20 learners at a level have a timed full section within 30 days of a rating reading, the row adds 'Measured: median 620 (n 34)' from R16 estimate.

OTHER PLACES:
- Overview 'Your stats' and Me's Rating tile (R31): 'Level 4 · 1,084 ≈ 520–600 Math'.
- 'Next level: +38 rating ≈ 4 hard rights at your level' = ceil(gap / (K × (1 − E_hard))).
- Target line: 'Your 650 target ≈ Level 6 (1,401+)', the inverse of band().
- Season card: 'Season goal: Level 4 → 6 by Oct 3', pre-filled from the target.

ACCEPTANCE:
- par for R_s = 1100 against three 1100-rated slots of 10/20/30 points is 30.
- band(R) is monotonic in R and capped at 580 on the lower route (server/checks/s8.py).
- The lobby par equals result.par after finish.
proposals.beats: They rank Contest Points and 'Overall Score' only. There is no level, no expectation for a student's level, and nothing that says what a contest result means on the SAT scale. Their profile shows Global Rank 128 with no contests played. The spec as written has a 1–10 level against item Elo, but it isn't tied to a score, so 'Level 4' means nothing to a student with a 650 target.
proposals.needs: S8: item_ratings and rating as specced, plus compete.par_for(sitting) and compete.band(R). scoring.py: _interpolate, ROUTE_UP_AT, MOCK_HALF_BAND, LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING (read only). blueprint.slots. F4: R16 estimate for the measured check. S1: Me Rating tile (R31) reads band(). Better with the whole-bank item calibration (parity gap 'field stats'), so par is right from day one.

proposals.title: Weekly leagues by level, scored on contest points plus fixes that held
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: every week they race about 30 students near their own level for a place. League points come from ranked contests plus mistakes that stayed fixed and points won back in Rematches. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: a weekly race you can actually win is the proven way to sustain daily practice. A global board is a race a 520 student can never win, so they stop. Counting held fixes means the race rewards learning, not only showing up.

WEEK: ISO week, Mon 00:00 UTC to the next Mon, the same as the week boards.

PLACEMENT: your first ranked contest finish of the week places you.
- Divisions by level at that moment: D1 Levels 1–3 and Placing, D2 Levels 4–5, D3 Levels 6–7, D4 Levels 8–10.
- Leagues fill within a division in join order, up to 30 ('Levels 4–5 · League 3').
- A division with < 10 joiners by Wed 00:00 UTC merges into the adjacent division, lower one first. With few students at launch there is one league.

LEAGUE POINTS:
- ranked contest points (the Daily; a Sprint's best run of the week; Weekly or Final);
- +20 per check-in held (R9, any mode, the Encore included), capped at 10 a day;
- + points won back in Rematches (P1).
The breakdown is shown on hover or expand.

OVERVIEW: a side card, between Season and the leaderboard preview.
- k 'LEAGUE · LEVELS 4–5' + meta 'ends in 3d 4h'.
- '#6 of 28'.
- 5 rows around you, each with a gap: '12 to pass #5'. Top 3 are marked with the podium glyph.
- Link 'Full league ›'.

LEADERBOARD: scope option 'My league', with the period locked to Week.

WEEK CLOSE: lazily, on the first request after Monday 00:00 UTC.
- Standings are stored.
- The student gets an inbox item (U25): 'Last week: #3 of 28 in Levels 4–5 · League podium'.
- Achievements (R25): 'League podium' (top 3) and 'League win' (1st), tiered by count.

YOUR RANKINGS: a 'Leagues' table, Week | Division | Place | Points (contests · fixes · won back).

IDENTITY: R12 rules apply. Hidden students keep their place as 'Anonymous'.

DATA: league_members(week, league, division, learner, joined, PK(week, learner)) and league_weeks(week, standings JSON, closed).

ACCEPTANCE:
- 35 seeded D2 joiners → 2 leagues (30 + 5). With 4 D3 joiners on Wednesday, D3 merges into D2.
- League points = contest points + 20 × held checks (the cap is respected) + won-back points.
- A closed week's standings stay unchanged after a rating change.
proposals.beats: They have a single global/country board (Weekly / Monthly / Yearly × Contest Points | Overall Score). It was empty on both walks, and it ranks only people who are already strong. The spec as written adds Near me and groups, but still no grouping by level and no weekly race that a mid-level student can win. Its points count only contest answers, never learning that lasted.
proposals.needs: S8: levels/rating, league placement and the close. F4: schema for league_members and league_weeks (§2.5), R9 check-in events. P1: won-back points. P2: Encore feeds the checks. S1: U25 inbox item and achievements through R25. R12: board identity.

proposals.title: Domain ratings, and the next step they point to
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: contests give them four ratings (Algebra, Advanced Math, Problem-Solving & Data Analysis, Geometry & Trig), each with a modelled band. The domain weakest relative to their target gets a one-tap drill and names the next contest that trains it. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: a single rating hides where the points are. A precise read per domain tells the student where the next 30 minutes pay most.

DATA:
- learners.ratings JSON {domain: {r, n}}, updated in compete.rate() beside the overall rating on every rated answer.
- Same E against the item rating. K = 32 until that domain's n ≥ 15, then 12. Provisional under 15.

YOUR RANKINGS, new card 'By domain', 4 rows. Each row has:
- the domain glyph and name;
- a 32 px level badge + rating;
- the modelled band from P4's band() restricted to that domain's items;
- a bar against the field median;
- '▲ 22 in 30 days';
- n.
Provisional rows read 'Placing · 6 of 15'.

TOP LINE: 'Weakest for your 650 target: Geometry & Trig (Level 3 ≈ 480–560; 650 needs Level 6).'
Actions:
- pill 'Practise Geometry & Trig · 10' → {topics: that domain's skills, adaptive: true, count: 10};
- quiet 'Sprint · Geometry week starts in 9 days' (from the Sprint theme rotation), with 'Add to calendar'.

CONTEST RESULT: the Rating tile expands to per-domain deltas, 'Algebra +18 · Geometry −6'.

LEADERBOARD: the Domain select is enabled for the Rating metric (it ranks domain ratings) as well as Points and Right.

ME: the Skills card (S1) may show the domain level beside mastery.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A rated right answer on an Algebra item moves ratings.Algebra.r and the overall rating, and leaves the other domains unchanged.
- /api/leaderboard?metric=rating&domain=Algebra ranks by ratings.Algebra.r.
- 'Weakest' picks the domain with the largest gap between its band centre and the target.
proposals.beats: They have no rating. Their Time Analysis splits only by difficulty, and their leaderboard has no domain filter. The spec as written has one overall rating, and its domain filter is disabled for Rating, so contests never tell a student which domain to work on.
proposals.needs: S8: compete.rate() and the leaderboard. P4: band(). F5: the domain → skills map from the practice builder. S1: optional Skills-card display. F4: learners.ratings column (§2.5).

proposals.title: Trap Tuesday: a Daily built around one misconception habit
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: on Tuesdays the Daily names one habit and its tell before starting, for example 'Answered a different quantity than asked' with the tell 'Before you pick, reread what exactly is asked'. Every question carries that trap as a distractor, across different skills. The result shows how often they fell for it against the field, then offers 'Drill this habit · 8'. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: telling one trap apart across contexts (interleaved by misconception, not by topic) transfers to unseen test questions far better than fixing one question type at a time. Rehearsing the named tell turns it into a checking routine for test day.

BUILD:
- Tuesday is the student's local day, like the Daily. The ladder is kept: 3E/4M/3H, domains 3/3/2/2, grid-ins at 4 and 8.
- Slot templates are drawn only from templates that have a reason in the week's family (U6's 11 families, habits.py).
- Twins are drawn with want={template: family regex}, so every student's seed shows that trap option.
- A grid-in slot is family-bound only if its template's spr_mistakes match. Otherwise it is a normal slot, left out of the trap stats and marked 'not part of the trap' in review.
- Family of the week: the ISO week number walks the 11 families in order, skipping any family with < 10 slot-feasible templates (checked by habits.py at startup).

LOBBY: k 'TRAP TUESDAY' + the family name + the tell in italics. The rules and ranking are unchanged.

RESULT PANEL: a line 'The trap: fell for it 2 of 8 · field 27%'. In review, the family option is labelled on every question. Pill 'Drill this habit · 8' (U6 source 'habit').

FIELD REVIEW: 'How the field answered' groups by misconception, as specced.

ACHIEVEMENT (R25): 'Trap-proof Tuesday', no falls on 4 Tuesdays.

TODAY CARD: 'Trap Tuesday · Answered a different quantity'.

ACCEPTANCE:
- habits.py prints ≥ 1 feasible family.
- A Tuesday daily's 10 canonical slots each regenerate (for 2 different learners' twins) with an option whose reason matches the family regex, grid-in exceptions aside.
- The result carries trap {family, fell, of, field_share}.
proposals.beats: Their options are explained in prose ('Distractor Analysis') but never tagged. They can't build a contest around a misconception, total who fell for it, or tell a student which habit caught them across topics. The spec as written sets Daily slots by domain and difficulty only.
proposals.needs: F5: server/habits.py families (U6) and drill 'want'. S8: daily slot builder variant in compete.ensure, and result.trap. S3: Today card label. S1: achievement through R25. T-bank: better spr_mistakes coverage widens the grid-in slots (open question 11).

proposals.title: Ghost races: race your best, a board rival, a friend's link or your par
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: they race a ghost on twin questions and watch it progress live. The ghost can be their own best Sprint, a named row on a board, a friend's shared result, or a 'par ghost' at their level. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: racing a near-peer or your own best sustains effort when few people are online, and a new free site's boards will be thin for months. Every race is extra retrieval on the same skills with new numbers.

GHOST: a finished sitting's per-slot marks and answer-clock times (attempts.sms), read by compete.ghost(sid).

PAR GHOST: for each slot it is right when E_i ≥ 0.5, and its time is the field median for the slot.

ENTRY POINTS:
- Sprint result: 'Race your best · 240'.
- Board row menu (⋯): 'Race', on public rows only, once you have finished your ranked sitting or the contest has closed.
- Copy result: the link becomes …/compete/contest/?id=daily-2026-09-23&race=<pid>.
- Lobby: quiet 'Race par'.

RUNNER: a two-lane bar under the top bar (S4 hook).
- 'You 5 ✓ · 120 | Ada 6 ✓ · 140 at this point'.
- After each verdict: 'Ada: ✓ in 0:48'.
- Sprint: the ghost's right count ticks up at its own answer times while the clock runs.

RANKED OR NOT:
- If the race is your first sitting of a live contest, it is your ranked sitting. Twins mean the ghost reveals nothing about your numbers.
- Otherwise it is a ghost sitting: unranked, with 'would have placed'.

RESULT: 'Beat Ada by 30 pts', or 'Ada by 10: she was 1:12 faster on Q7'. Sprint adds 'Race again'.

SHARED-LINK LANDING: the contest title, the sharer's board name (or 'A student' when hidden), 'Beat 170', and pill 'Race'. A first visit mints a learner code as usual.

ACCEPTANCE:
- GET /api/contest/{cid}?race=<pid> returns ghost {marks, sms} only when the target is public and the rule above holds, and 403 otherwise.
- A race started on a live daily by a learner with no sitting is ranked.
- A par ghost's right slots equal those with E ≥ 0.5.
proposals.beats: They have no head-to-head, no retakes of a ranked contest ('One attempt per contest'), and their Share called navigator.share, which froze the page. The spec as written has Compare after the fact and 'Challenge a friend' as a new private contest, but never a live race against a specific sitting or against your own best.
proposals.needs: F4: attempts.sms. S4: runner header lane through R28's compete.state_extra. S8: compete.ghost, the race param on start, and the row-menu item. P4: par for the par ghost. F1: UI.copyText link change. R12: public rows only.

proposals.title: Season Final → your last week, planned from it
proposals.beats: Their 'Seasonal' is only a contest label, and their AI study plan failed 3 of 3 times on the walk. The only reschedule is 'move later this week'. Nothing links a rehearsal to the week before the exam. The spec as written ends the Final at a band and a rank.
proposals.needs: S7: a Plan API to write tasks for specific dates (plan.py) and the rest-day rule. P1: result.left. P3: time sinks and par. F5: U6 tells. S5: R7 per-question time in the test window. F1: print CSS. F1: UI.ics(event) for the no-plan fallback.

proposals.title: Squad streak and a weekly class cup
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: in a class or a small friends' squad they keep a shared Daily streak that stays alive only if everyone does the Daily. They see who has done it today and can nudge whoever hasn't. Classes compete weekly on points per member. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: social accountability is one of the strongest adherence levers. A streak that other people depend on gets a student to do the Daily on the days they would skip, and days practised is what drives the score.

SQUAD STREAK, for any class (R4):
- With 2–10 current members: consecutive days on which every member finished that day's Daily, each on their own local day.
- With 11 or more: consecutive days on which ≥ 75% did.
- A member's spare day (U16) counts as done for them.
- Computed by compete.squad_streak(class).

OVERVIEW G CARD, per class:
- member dots (✓ done / half-filled in progress / empty not yet), named inside the class as R12 allows;
- 'Squad streak 6 · best 11';
- a quiet 'Nudge' on each not-yet member. It sends an inbox item (U25): 'Ada nudged you: today's Daily closes 11:59 PM'. Limit: 1 per sender per member per day. Not shown for members who have left.

CLASS CUP:
- Weekly, for classes with ≥ 5 members active that week.
- Ranked by mean league points per active member (P5 points; contest points if leagues are off), so class size doesn't decide it.
- Leaderboard scope 'Classes' lists class rows: rank, class name, active members, mean points.
- The class owner's view shows the class's place.

ACHIEVEMENT (R25): 'Squad week', a 7-day squad streak.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A 3-member class where all 3 finished today's and yesterday's Daily → squad_streak 2.
- One member missing today → the streak holds at 2 until their day ends, then 0 (spares aside).
- A second nudge from one sender to one member on one day → 429.
proposals.beats: Their classes and homework are hidden, with no social layer. Their boards are global or country only. The spec as written has group boards and group contests, but nothing that makes one student's practice matter to the others day to day.
proposals.needs: S2: classes/members (R4). S1: U25 inbox (the nudge) and achievements. F4: U16 spares in progress.days(). P5: league points for the cup. S8: squad_streak and the 'Classes' leaderboard scope.

proposals.title: Call your score: calibration before each contest
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: before the Daily or the Weekly they optionally predict how many they will get right. Afterwards they see 'Called 7 · got 5', and over time how far their calls run high or low. WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: overconfident students under-review and skip checking. Seeing your own calibration error corrects it, which improves test-day calls on when to double-check and when to move on, and how study time gets spent.

LOBBY:
- 'Call it' stepper 0–N (N = the question count), blank by default.
- Helper 'How many will you get right? It doesn't change your points.'
- Stored in sessions.result.call at start. Locked once the first question is served.

RESULT: a line 'Called 7 · got 5'.

YOUR RANKINGS, a 'Calibration' tile in the Performance summary:
- mean (call − right) over the last 12 calls ('your calls run 1.4 high');
- 'within ±1: 5 of 12';
- a 12-dot strip, each dot placed at call − right.

ACHIEVEMENT (R25): 'Called it', exact 5 times.

POINTS AND RANK: no effect.

ACCEPTANCE:
- POST start with call=7, then 5 right → result.call 7 and history shows 'Called 7 · got 5'.
- A call sent after the first serve → 409.
- The tile's mean equals the mean of the stored differences.
proposals.beats: They collect no prediction or confidence data in contests or anywhere else. Shell-me rejected tagging confidence on every practice question because students won't tap it. One stepper tap per contest is cheap enough that students will do it.
proposals.needs: S8 only: the start endpoint, the result line and the rankings tile. S1: achievement through R25.

parity_gaps.feature: Contest scoring: difficulty points plus a speed bonus
parity_gaps.spec_says: 10/20/30 for each easy/medium/hard right, +5 for a right answer within 95 s, +10 for finishing with nothing skipped or voided.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It has the same shape as their 'points by difficulty plus a speed bonus'. A flat 95 s is trivial to meet on easy questions and pushes students to rush hard ones, which is the opposite of real module pacing.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Pace par by tier: easy 60 s, medium 95 s, hard 130 s. It sums to exactly 950 s for the Daily and 2,090 s for a module. Each template moves to its own median once it has ≥ 30 first-try rights (P3's compete.par). The bonus becomes '+5 within pace par', so it teaches banking time on easy questions and spending it on hard ones.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Points · Rating · Questions right · Test score. Rating adds a Change column for the period.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Every metric ranks current ability or volume, like their Contest Points | Overall Score. A student improving fast from a low start never moves up the board.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a 'vs par' metric: Σ (base − par) over ranked sittings, min 3 (P4). The Rating metric gets a 'Sort: Rating | Change' toggle, so 'Most improved' is a real board with its own podium. The Test score metric gets U11's Climb: estimate gain within your starting-band cohort, shown when n ≥ 20, one source through compete.climb.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Three cards in the order 2 · 1 · 3 with heights 132/156/116, showing the metric value and 'accuracy · avg time'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their top-3 hero. Almost no student is ever on it, so for most students it motivates nothing.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Under the podium, a 'Your race' strip: the 3 rows just above you with their gaps ('12 pts · about one medium right') and your movement since last week ('▲ 4'). Climb and vs-par boards get their own podium, so someone at every level can reach one.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Rank | Student + level | metric | Accuracy | Avg time | Contests.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It matches their RANK / USERNAME / ACCURACY / TIME with more columns, but a row tells you nothing about yourself.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a 'Gap' column relative to you ('+34' / '−12'), a movement arrow since last week's snapshot on each row (U11's rank_snapshot), and row actions 'Race' (P8) and 'Compare'.

parity_gaps.feature: Hub leaderboard preview and 'Your stats' card
parity_gaps.spec_says: E: THIS WEEK · POINTS, top 5 + your row. D: rating + level + 6 rank tiles (week, all-time, country, points, contests, best finish).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It repeats their Global Leaderboard card and Your Contest Stats (global rank): the world's top 5 and static ranks with no direction.
parity_gaps.upgrade: E shows your league, or Near me when leagues are off: 5 rows around you with gaps. D's tiles carry '▲ since last week'. Rating reads 'Level 4 · 1,084 ≈ 520–600 Math', plus 'Next level +38 ≈ 4 hard rights' (P4). All-time rank also shows the top-% trend.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Voids on the tab hidden ≥ 5 s, copy/cut/paste, or pagehide while a question is open. Optional fullscreen.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their rule with a 5 s grace. Voiding on copy punishes copying an expression into the built-in calculator, which the real digital SAT's Desmos invites. With twins, copying a stem leaks nothing to another student.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Drop copy/cut as triggers. A paste into the embedded calculator (event target inside the Desmos host) never voids; a paste into the answer field or any other element does, and so does the tab hidden ≥ 5 s, which covers pasting into an outside solver. Add 'Send to calculator' on every math expression in the stem and choices, which types it into Desmos. The result shows 'Integrity: 0 voids' as part of the Ranked line.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Right / Wrong / Skipped / Voided, the points breakdown (base + pace + finish), topic mastery bars, mistakes opened and closed.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: The counts are their Score / Correct / Incorrect / Skipped / Voided, and the mastery bars are the practice summary. None of it says what cost the points or what to do about it.
parity_gaps.upgrade: P1's 'Points left on the table': points by misconception, pace, skip and void, and finish bonus, each with 'Fix it · 3' (a worked twin, then 2 want-matched twins) and a Rematch at +48 h.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Toggle By difficulty / By domain / Right vs wrong / Under pressure: your median vs the field median and a 95 s line.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is a richer version of their 'average seconds per answered question, by difficulty' plus 'under pressure'. It shows numbers but no action, and uses one flat line for every tier.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Each row carries U7's quadrant action: Speed drill / Careful set / Learn it untimed / Keep warm. The flat 95 s line becomes the tier pace par. Add 'Time in sinks per contest' and 'Banked on easy' trends over the last 10 contests (P3).

parity_gaps.feature: 'How you placed in a contest' picker
parity_gaps.spec_says: A select of finished contests showing a mini board (top 5 + you ± 2) and 'Open contest ›'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their 'Contest Leaderboard: pick a contest you've finished', and the History table below it repeats the same list.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Fold it into Contest history. Each row expands in place to the mini board, your points-left rows and the Rematch status. A placing-trend sparkline per kind sits above the table, and the separate control goes.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Filters for kind and sort. Columns Date | Contest | Score | R·W·S·V | Points | Time | Rank | Top % | Rating Δ | Ranked | Review.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their Your Contest History with more columns. It records the past but gives the student nothing left to do.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A 'Follow-up' column: '3 misses · won back 2/3 · 1 open' or 'Rematch opens Thu'. A filter 'Open follow-ups (n)' turns history into a to-do list, and each open item has a 'Fix it' button (P1).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Compete's unique badges (pace-setter, top-ten, weekly-4, sprinter, dress-rehearsal, season-top-10, level-5, level-8, all-rounder) go through R25's engine.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: A progress grid of rank and volume badges is what their Badge Progress card promises. It rewards placing and grinding, not learning.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add learning-behaviour ladders through R25: 'Won back' (Rematch questions, P1), 'Kept' (Encore check-ins held, P2), 'Beat par' (5 days in a row, P4), 'Trap-proof Tuesday' (P7), 'Called it' (P11), 'League podium' (P5) and 'Squad week' (P10). Each has U13's Go button that starts the drill that advances it.

parity_gaps.feature: Field statistics (field % right, median time, option spread, item ratings)
parity_gaps.spec_says: Aggregated from ranked contest sittings only. The verdict's '62% of 37 got this right' appears once ≥ 5 have answered. item_ratings calibrate from rated contest answers.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: On a new free site the field is tiny: the dev DB holds 3 challenge sittings. So most verdicts show nothing, and ratings and par start from guesses. Their boards were empty on both walks for the same reason.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Back the field with every first-try answer on the same (template, tier) in any mode (practice, tests, contests; R8 exclusions apply). The line reads '64% of 1,284 first tries on this type · today 5 of 7'. item_ratings calibrate from the same answers (weight 1 for contest, 0.5 elsewhere). Student ratings stay contest-only. Median times use sms/ms, so par, pace par and the field trace are right from day one.

parity_gaps.feature: 'Practice for it' on an upcoming contest
parity_gaps.spec_says: A 10-question drill over the contest's domains.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is generic topic practice, the same idea as their 'More practice'.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Personalised prep inside the contest's blueprint (never its hidden slot templates). It is weighted to your two lowest domain ratings (P6) and your open traps in those domains, with the tiers matching the ladder. The lobby shows your par before and after the prep ('par 105 → 110').

parity_gaps.feature: Private and group contests with an owner results table
parity_gaps.spec_says: The creator picks skills, difficulty, format, clock, window, twins, reveal and strict. The owner gets per-question marks and CSV.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their hidden teacher dashboard (assign, due dates, results), just free and visible.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Two new sources in the create sheet: 'From the class's traps' (the 10 misconceptions most members hold open, twins drawn with want) and 'From my open mistakes' for friends. The results table adds a class-misconception ranking ('41% fell for: inverted the slope') with 'Assign a Rematch' to the members who fell. It becomes a per-member P1 Rematch with a due time.

parity_gaps.spec_says: 'Copy result' copies plain text with a square strip and the contest link. 'Challenge a friend' opens the create sheet.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It replaces their share sheet (which froze the page), but it is still a brag message that asks nothing of the reader.
parity_gaps.upgrade: The copied link carries &race=<pid>. A friend who opens it races the sharer's ghost on twins, ranked if it is their first sitting of a live contest (P8). The copied text's last line reads 'Beat 170: <link>'.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A repeating .ics (RRULE:FREQ=DAILY, default 17:00) titled 'SAT Freshman · Daily Challenge'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is a static alarm, only marginally better than their 'Preferred time: Evening', which does nothing. It says the same thing every day.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Route it through U18: the subscribed feed's daily event names what's due ('Daily + Encore: 2 check-ins + Rematch 5 · about 22 min'), and push (when VAPID is set) sends 'Daily closes in 2 h' only on days you haven't done it. The static .ics stays as the fallback.

parity_gaps.feature: Ranked pill and percentile on the score report
parity_gaps.spec_says: R16: a percentile among each learner's first standard sitting of the same kind, shown when n ≥ 20, with a Ranked / Not ranked pill.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their 'N% scored at or below you on their first attempt' and 'Practice test — not ranked'. A site-internal percentile means little to a student aiming at a college's range.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Beside it, the College Board's published user percentile range for the band's two ends ('610–690 ≈ 81st–92nd percentile of SAT takers'), from a yearly table in estimate.py (F4). Also 'Among students with your 650 target: 58th', shown when n ≥ 20.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Ten stat tiles plus a Top % / Rating chart over 30 contests, 90 days or all.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their Performance Summary with more tiles: a dashboard of numbers with no explanation of what moved them.
parity_gaps.upgrade: A 'What changed' line above the tiles: 'Since last week: rating +46 (Algebra +60, Geometry −12) · biggest gain: fixed "inverted the slope" · biggest loss: 2 time sinks in Geometry'. Each part links to its drill, and the line is computed from P6's domain deltas, P1's won-back items and P3's sinks.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Kind icon, title, window, facts ('22 questions · 35 min · your own twin questions · 128 in'), status chip and action.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their active-contests list, always populated, but it doesn't say why a student should enter.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Each row adds a 'Trains' line ('module pace and routing', 'Algebra fluency', 'this week's trap') and your par with last result ('par 290 · last week 260').

parity_gaps.spec_says: Rows for Everyone / Country / each group, columns Week / Month / Season / All, cells '#12 of 340 · top 4%'.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their 'Your Rankings: Global rank, Contests played', expanded into a grid of static positions.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Each cell adds movement ('▲ 3') and the gap to the next place ('7 pts to #11') from U11's snapshots. A 'My league' row (P5) and a 'Climb' row (U11) join the table.
